plain_words.what: We wrote one page per part: what it is for, what it decides, and how we would know it is healthy.
plain_words.decided: Three pages. Each names the rules it enforces and the words it owns.
plain_words.assumed: The cutoff time is a business rule that lives in subscriptions and nowhere else.
plain_words.riskiest: If the cutoff is really a fulfilment rule (when the warehouse must know), it is written in the wrong place.

canvases.purpose: Subscriptions decides which meals each household receives each week and keeps the standing order alive: it opens, pauses and cancels subscriptions and locks a week's choice before the cutoff, so that households keep choosing (G1). It does not charge the card (billing) or pack the box (fulfilment).
business_decisions: A week can be chosen once; a second choice for the same week is rejected
Choices lock at the weekly cutoff; after it, default meals are assigned
assumptions: [define A1] Fixture: metrics are illustrative targets
verification_metrics: Business (G1): active subscriptions grow month on month; weekly choice completed by >90% of active households before cutoff
Boundary: zero cross-module reads of subscription tables from billing/fulfilment (CI check)
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Execution context: it owns the subscription aggregate and takes the household's commands directly; the weekly cutoff is enforced here, not downstream.

canvases.purpose: Billing takes the money for a chosen week: whenever meals are chosen it charges the household's card through Stripe and tells the rest of the system the week is paid. It owns no product rules — a failed charge is reported back to subscriptions, which decides what to do.
business_decisions: A week is charged exactly once, on meals-chosen; retries are idempotent on subscriptionId+week
A declined card pauses the subscription and releases the week
assumptions: [define A1] Fixture: metrics are illustrative targets
verification_metrics: Business: failed charges retried and resolved within 24h for >95% of weeks
Boundary: every Stripe call goes through the PaymentGateway ACL (fitness test)
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Execution context around a bought capability: it reacts to meals-chosen and executes the charge through the Stripe ACL; no model of its own beyond the charge record.

canvases.purpose: Fulfilment turns a paid week into a physical box: it builds the picking list, packs the box in the warehouse and hands it to the courier with tracking, so the household gets what it chose. It never queries subscriptions; everything it needs arrives on week-charged.
business_decisions: A box is packed only for a charged week
A box is shipped only after it is packed; tracking is recorded on shipment
assumptions: [define A1] Fixture: metrics are illustrative targets
verification_metrics: Business: boxes packed within 12h of week-charged for >99% of weeks; mis-picks <0.5%
Boundary: fulfilment reads recipe/picking data only from the week-charged payload or its own projection
canvases.domain_roles_rationale: Execution context: packers act on it directly and it owns the physical box's lifecycle; it consumes week-charged and never queries subscriptions.
